name: Caséta Smart Bridge (US)

radios.note: Lutron says the hub plugs into a LAN port on the router with the included Ethernet cable and doesn't use Wi-Fi. Devices talk over Lutron Clear Connect RF, which is not in the radio list, so only Ethernet is recorded.

matter.note: No Matter claim found for the Smart Bridge.

apple_home.note: Lutron says HomeKit needs a second-generation Smart Bridge (L-BDG2) or Smart Bridge PRO; the HomeKit setup code goes into the Lutron app.

google_home.note: Link the Caséta Wireless service in the Google Home app.

alexa.note: Enable the Lutron Caséta skill in the Alexa app and sign in with your Lutron account.

smartthings.note: No official source found in search results.

home_assistant.note: Official Lutron Caséta integration; the docs list the L-BDG2-WH Smart Hub and the Smart Bridge PRO.

hubRequired.note: It is the hub. Caséta dimmers and switches work with Pico remotes without it, but app control, schedules, scenes and smart-speaker integration need it.

localControl.note: Lutron says the hub doesn't use Wi-Fi, so local control keeps working during an internet outage.

deviceProtocols.note: Lutron Clear Connect RF, to Caséta dimmers, switches, fan controls, Pico remotes and sensors.

maxDevices.note: Lutron says up to 75 Caséta devices per hub. Some retailer listings still give the older 50.

summary: The Caséta Smart Bridge (L-BDG2) connects Lutron Caséta dimmers, switches, Pico remotes and shades to your router by Ethernet. Lutron's devices then work with Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and Home Assistant.

caveats: Lutron now calls it the Caséta Smart Hub; the L-BDG2 is the standard model and the Smart Bridge Pro is separate.
Only second-generation bridges (L-BDG2 and Pro 2) work with Apple HomeKit.
The bridge needs an Ethernet cable to the router; Lutron devices use Clear Connect RF, not Wi-Fi or Zigbee.
